messages:
marie (runtime): Heads-up — noticed an FP8 FlashAttention variant producing unstable softmax outputs on the canary run. Some generations end up with extremely large logits or NaN mid-sequence.

akshay: ugh. any idea if it's numeric or a kernel bug?

marie (runtime): Looks numeric + kernel-selection interaction. When the selector chooses flash-attn-quantized (fp8 path) for long prefix lengths the softmax exponent explodes on ~0.01% of requests. If we force fallback to the stable fused softmax the problem disappears.

noah: can you paste the minimal repro + perf numbers?

marie (runtime): repro command (local) — run on the canary model and the seqlen pattern that reproduces: 

```
# reproduce workload
python -m tools.run_infer --model magneto-v1 --batch 1 --seq-lens 1024,128,128,1024 --use-fp8-quant --kernel=auto
```

logs show repeated lines like: `softmax exp overflow at head 3, qk_scale=8.192e+02` then `logits NaN` and token probabilities collapse. When I force `--kernel=stable-fused` no overflow.

akshay: do we have perf counters / flamegraphs? is it a latency regression when we flip back to stable?

perf-bot: quick snapshot (canary region):
- flash-attn-fp8 (auto selector picked): p50 9.2ms p95 28.7ms p99 84.1ms; error-rate 0.12% (NaN/logit failure)
- fused-stable: p50 11.5ms p95 30.1ms p99 76.4ms; error-rate 0.00%

ank: so flash is faster on p50 but we're seeing higher p99 flakiness and correctness issues.

noah: hypothesis: KV cache page boundary + chunked matmul changes exponent range. FP8 quantization reduces dynamic range; combined with different tiling the max(Q*K) becomes bigger causing softmax to overflow. Might be sensitive to batch/batching heuristic too.

marie (runtime): confirmed: repro only with specific sequence-length mix that triggers a different batching path + paged KV crossing. If I change batching heuristics to avoid splitting within heads, it rarely reproduces.

jen: we need short-term and long-term fixes:
1) short: add a guard in kernel selector to avoid choosing fp8-flash for requests where seqlen pattern causes page crossing heuristics to flip (i.e., prefer stable-fused if KV pages > 1 and seqlen variance > threshold).
2) medium: add a numeric clamp to softmax exp inside fp8 path: `exp_clip = min(exp(arg), EXP_CLIP)` and lower default EXP_CLIP for fp8 kernels.
3) long: add exhaustive fuzz tests for varying seqlen mixes, batching orders, and KV-cache warm/cold states in CI.

akshay: agree. also we should add detection at runtime to count softmax overflows and auto-fallback per-request (fast fallback policy) instead of whole-canary rollback. That will reduce blast radius.

marie (runtime): implemented a quick guard in selector: if (kv_pages > 1 && seq_variance > 512) -> pick stable-fused. Pushed branch: https://git.redwood/magneto/rt/branches/exp/fp8-guard-1756 (WIP). Can run canary with this.

perf-bot: perf diff when gating on that condition (canary subset):
- flash-attn-pick-rate down from 72% -> 53%
- p50 unchanged, p99 improved by ~6ms, error-rate dropped to 0.01%

noah: good. We still need the exp-clamp in kernel code — that's cheap and protects against other weird tilings. marie can you add a tiny patch to softmax kernel: `if (is_fp8_path) x = clamp(x, -MAX_LOG, MAX_LOG)` before exp?

marie (runtime): will do, but want to land selector guard first so fewer customers hit kernel. Planning to bundle kernel clamp + unit tests in next PR.

jen: assignment/timeline:
- marie: land selector guard to canary today (BLOCKER -> canary), add runtime softmax overflow counter metric (count per-model) — due EOD
- marie/noah: kernel-exp clamp + unit tests + CI fuzz harness for seqlen mixes — PR by EOW
- akshay: monitor canary and prepare easy rollback (pin model to stable-fused) if error-rate > 0.05%

sre-bot: Canaries alerted: monitor slack #incidents if auto-fallback triggers > 10/min.

marie (runtime): notes on tests I'll add: unit test will brute-force random seqlen arrays and ensure no NaN for 1000 trials on both warm and cold KV cache modes. Also add a targeted test that forces head-chunk boundary alignment flipping.

akshay: thanks. one more thing — pls capture kernel selector decision trace in debug logs for a sample of requests (not all) so we can audit path selection + batching heuristics when a failure occurs.

marie (runtime): yep adding selector trace sample (1/1000) that logs seqlens, kv_pages, kernel_chosen, quant_mode, tiling info.

noah: happy to help review the fuzz harness and the numeric clamp. quick sanity: ensure the clamp doesn't bias stable cases (add regression threshold checks in tests).

marie (runtime): thanks all — rolling the guard to canary now. will post canary link and follow-ups here. :rocket:

jen: good plan. postmortem template ready in #postmortems if needed. keep me posted. :thumbsup:
